## Architecture guardrails (archfit)

- Before you add an import across modules, ask: `archfit policy can-import <file> <target>`.
  A `denied` answer names the rule and the repair. `unconstrained` is not permission.
- Before you finish, run `archfit check --format agent` and follow `next_action`.
  `none` is a correct finish, even with exit code 2.
- Never edit `ddd.archfit.yaml`, the baseline, waivers, or labels to make a check pass.
  Ask the architecture owner instead.

### Modules

| Module | Paths | Layer | Owner | Public | Depends on | Visible to |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `catalog` | `internal/catalog/**` | domain | team-catalog | `internal/catalog/contract` | any | any |
| `notifications` | `internal/notifications/**` | infrastructure | team-platform | `internal/notifications/contract` | any | any |
| `ordering` | `internal/ordering/**` | domain | team-ordering | `internal/ordering/contract` | any | any |
| `pricing` | `internal/pricing/**` | domain | team-pricing | `internal/pricing/contract` | any | any |

Layers, inner to outer: `domain`, `application`, `infrastructure`. A layer may import only itself and layers inner to it.

### Rules that block

All code:

- `contexts_via_contract`: may import another module only through that module's `public` paths.
- `layer_direction`: must not import a layer outer to its own.
- `no_module_cycles`: must not close a dependency cycle between declared modules.
